transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello Dr. Smith, I'm Roy, and my primary doctor referred me to you because lately I jump out of my skin at the smallest noises, like I’m bracing for something bad to happen all the time. It really hit home during a woodworking class recently when I startled so violently at a dropped tool that it embarrassed me and made me realize how on-edge I've become in everyday situations. I'm just hoping to figure out why I'm feeling this way.
Did these feelings of being on edge and easily startled begin after a specific distressing or life-threatening event you experienced or witnessed?

Yes, it all started about 13 months ago during a sailboat race I was skippering when a sudden squall rolled in. A nearby boat capsized, and I watched one of their crew members get struck by the boom and thrown into the water. Just recalling the chaos of that storm and seeing him go under makes me feel incredibly tense and shaken up.
Since that incident 13 months ago, have you experienced these symptoms consistently throughout that entire time, or have there been periods where your symptoms improved or completely went away?

To be honest, it's been a constant thing ever since that storm last year, so it’s been a little over a year now. I haven't really had any breaks or times where the feeling went away or improved. It's just been hanging over me day in and day out.
